general_information.Pre-Requisite: Recommend to have knowledge of introductory electromagnetic theory and basic concepts of optics (PHY101); calculus and elementary differential equations (MAC101) in advance
general_information.Description: The course firstly gives students a basic overview of how optical communications blend into telecommunication systems. Then it describes details on the physical structures, constituent materials, attenuation behavior, light wave propagation mechanisms, and signal dispersion characteristics of the wide variety of optical fibers that exist. Thirdly, the course addresses the principles of optical sources and how couple two fibers to ensure a low optical power loss at the joints. Subsequently, the structures and responses of photodetectors as well as the principles of lightwave receivers are covered. Finally, digital transmission and its associated parameters on system performance are discussed. Topics are covered: Overview of Optical Fiber Communications; Optical Fibers: Structures, Waveguilding and Fabrication; Attenuation and Dispersion; Optical Sources; Power Launching and Coupling; Photodetectors; Optical Receiver Operation; Digital Links.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by an instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Constantly follow announcements on intranet/CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information.
general_information.Tools: Modeling and Simulation Tools: (suggestion) 1. Optiwave, http://www.optiwave.com (recommended) 2. RSoft Design Group, http://www.rsoftdesign.com 3. VPIsystems, http://www.vpiphotonics.com

assessments.Question Type: Do practice and simulation in class/lab
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Each lab activity can be assigned for every group of 3-4 students. 2. In every lab subject, there are various lessions, the instructor can assign different lessions to differen groups. 3. The lab manual can be download from the website: http://optiwave.com/category/products/system-and-amplifier-design/optisystem/optisystem-applications/ ---> OptiSystem Manuals-----> OptiSystem Tutorials 4. Analysis and Report: • Compare the results of the simulations and theory • Record your observations and explanations of differences in your lab report. 5. Your report should contain: • Cover page - Title of the lab - Course name - Your name and student number • Screen shots of layout and results, including eye diagrams • Written summary of your observations and your analysis
assessments.Note: - Reports must be submitted at the end of every pratical session. - Instructor should supervise everygroup's progress in the practical session to ensure all tasks done and no-cheating - The lab evaluation is averagely based on group progress in the practical sessions and the group reports. The scores should be finished before the final examination

assessments.Grading Guide: - Topics should be selected by a group of 3 students (group division should be done in the first slot) and submitted titles before slot 4. - Each topic should be done with the theory comprehesion, state-of-the-art technologies and proved by real examples containing images, software, tools and systems…... - Presentations are arranged along the course, starting from slot 10 and groups will present in turn.
assessments.Note: - Presentation: 20 mins per group - PPT slides must be made by group and every member must take park in one part to present - Additional documents from other sources are encouraged for further researches

assessments.Grading Guide: - Test 1: cover chapter 1-3 - Test 2: cover chapter 4-5 - Test 3: cover chapter 6-7 Each test should have both theory questions and numerial problems covering contents of every chapter equally

assessments.No Question: Part I: Multiple choice of 30 theorical questions Part II: Numerial Problems of 2-3 exercises
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All chapters; knowledge and skills of the course;
assessments.Note: Weight for multiple choice, is 40% and for exercise is 60%. No documents are accepted to bring into the examination room.
